name: hirayacoder
description: A fully offline, privacy-first AI coding agent powered by your local Ollama instance. Agentic on every model — even 1B.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: HirayaCoder can read, write, and delete workspace files and run permission-gated shell commands, so it requires a trusted workspace.

hirayacoder.ollama.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL of your local Ollama instance. **Must be a loopback address** (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, or `::1`) — HirayaCoder rejects any non-loopback host by design, so no code or context ever leaves your machine.

hirayacoder.ollama.requestTimeoutMs.description: How long to wait for a single Ollama request before aborting, in milliseconds.

hirayacoder.model.selected.description: The Ollama model HirayaCoder uses. Leave empty to auto-select the first installed model.

hirayacoder.model.liteTierMaxParams.markdownDescription: Models at or below this parameter count (in billions) always run the Tier B lite ReAct loop, **even if they advertise native tool-calling support**. Small models often claim tool support but are unreliable at multi-tool orchestration. Set to `0` to classify purely on advertised capability.

hirayacoder.inlineCompletion.enabled.markdownDescription: Suggest ghost-text completions while you type. **Off by default**: completions run against your local model on every typing pause, and on CPU-only inference a suggestion often arrives after you have already typed the line. Turn it on if your machine has a GPU or you are running a small, fast model.

hirayacoder.model.todoMinParams.markdownDescription: Smallest model (in billions of parameters) allowed to break a multi-part request into a TODO list and work through it one item at a time. The model must **also** report Ollama's `thinking` capability. Models below this still handle multi-part requests in a single pass — a model that cannot finish one item reliably does worse, not better, when given a list of them.

hirayacoder.model.tierOverrides.markdownDescription: Force a specific tier per model, bypassing auto-detection. Example: `{ "llama3.2:1b": "A" }`.

hirayacoder.model.recommendAboveParams.description: If an installed model exceeds this parameter count (in billions) and it is not the selected model, show a one-time, dismissible suggestion to switch to it.

enumDescriptions: Smallest context and step budget — fastest, least memory recall.
Balanced step budget with one up-front planning pass and moderate memory recall.
Largest step budget, re-planning checkpoints, and the deepest memory recall.
hirayacoder.thinkingCapacity.description: Controls step budget and how much persisted session memory is recalled per turn.

enumDescriptions: Full agentic loop — read, write, delete, and run scripts, subject to your permission settings.
Read-only exploration that produces a reviewable plan checklist. Write/delete/script tools are structurally unavailable.
Single-response Q&A with no agent loop and no tool calls at all.
hirayacoder.mode.description: Default mode for new chat messages.

hirayacoder.permissions.autoEdit.description: When off (default), every file write and delete requires explicit approval. When on, proposed edits apply automatically — still logged, still path-guarded.

hirayacoder.permissions.alwaysConfirmDel.markdownDescription: Ask before deleting a file **even when Auto Edit is on**. A wrong write is visible in the diff and recoverable; a wrong delete of an uncommitted file is not — and small models do misidentify delete targets. Turn this off only if you want Auto Edit to cover deletions too.

hirayacoder.permissions.autoApproveScrip.markdownDescription: When off (default), every shell command requires explicit approval. **Highest-risk setting** — commands still run only from the allow-listed binary set, but without a confirmation click.

hirayacoder.scripts.allowedBinaries.markdownDescription: Extra programs the agent may run, added to the built-in allow-list (`node`, `npm`, `git`, `pytest`, …). The model can never extend this list — only you can. Commands that reach the network or publish code (`git push`, `npm publish`) always require confirmation regardless of this setting.

hirayacoder.scripts.timeoutMs.description: How long a single agent-run command may take before it is terminated.

hirayacoder.security.protectedPaths.markdownDescription: Workspace-relative paths the agent may never write to or delete. Reads are still permitted. `.hirayacoder` is listed so the agent cannot rewrite its own audit log or memory.

hirayacoder.adaptation.enabled.markdownDescription: Let HirayaCoder learn from what happens in this workspace. Outcomes are recorded to `.hirayacoder/outcomes.jsonl` — model, tier, action, which guard refused it, how the session ended — and a model that trips the same guard repeatedly gets the matching correction added to its prompt. **Adaptation never touches permissions, path confinement, or the allow-list**: it only changes what the model is told, never what it is allowed to do. Run *Show Learned Adaptation* to see it, *Reset Learned Adaptation* to discard it.

hirayacoder.adaptation.hintThreshold.markdownDescription: How many times one model must trip the same guard before the matching correction is added to its prompt. Lower learns faster and spends more of a small model's prompt budget on corrections; one trip is an accident rather than a habit.

hirayacoder.statusBar.enabled.description: Show the HirayaCoder status bar item (connection state, active model, and tier).

hirayacoder.logLevel.description: Verbosity of the HirayaCoder output channel.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Each chat tab is a session with its own memory, kept in this workspace.

[Start a chat](command:hirayacoder.openChat)

Runs entirely on your machine through Ollama.

scripts.test: npm run lint && npm run test:unit
scripts.test:all: npm run lint && npm run test:unit && npm run test:integration
